name: Household Ledger - List Budget Webhook Agent

parameters.content:
## SETUP TODOs
1. Replace `documentId` on every Google Sheets node below with your Household Ledger spreadsheet ID (see household-ledger-sheets-schema.md)
2. Connect your Google Sheets credential (reused the same credential ID as your BNS workflows below — adjust if this is a different Google account)
3. Activate this workflow, then grab the Production webhook URL from the Webhook node — that's what the mobile app POSTs to
4. Create the `LastSavedList` tab (see household-ledger-sheets-schema.md) — same columns as `ShoppingList`. Needed for the `finalize`/`recall` pair below.

Expected POST body:
`{ "action": "get" }`
`{ "action": "upsert", "item": "Basmati Rice", "category": "Pantry", "store": "Walmart", "price": 9.52, "qty": 1, "cadence": "Week" }`
`{ "action": "remove", "item": "Basmati Rice" }`
`{ "action": "clear" }` — empties every ShoppingList row (keeps the header)
`{ "action": "finalize" }` — doesn't change ShoppingList; sends a Telegram summary of the current list + total, and snapshots the list into LastSavedList (clear+append) so it survives a later `clear`. Same response shape as `get`.
`{ "action": "recall" }` — added 2026-08-09, upserts every row from LastSavedList into ShoppingList (merges on top, matched on item — same as a normal upsert), letting next week's list start from last week's finalized one. Same response shape as `get`.

Response: `{ "list": [...rows], "total": 42.10, "budget": 200, "remaining": 157.90 }`

Confirmed live 2026-08-08: Clear All and Save List (finalize+Telegram) both working end-to-end, Send Finalize Summary's real bot credential wired with On Error set to Continue.

SETUP TODO for `recall`/snapshot (2026-08-09, not yet applied live): the new LastSavedList-clearing chain (`Get LastSavedList Rows to Clear` → ... → `Snapshot to LastSavedList`) has `onError: continueRegularOutput` pre-set in this file rather than left to configure live, since we now know that field name — worth a quick visual double-check in the node Settings tab once live, same as was done for Send Finalize Summary. Also double check the `rowsToDelete` field name on `Clear LastSavedList Rows` the same way it was verified on `Clear ShoppingList Rows`.

nodes.name: Find Row to Remove
nodes.notes: alwaysOutputData so a genuine no-match (item already removed, name mismatch, etc.) passes through as an empty placeholder instead of halting this branch -- see Found Row to Remove? gate right after, added 2026-08-08.

nodes.name: Found Row to Remove?
nodes.notes: Fixes the documented 'if the item wasn't found, this will error -- acceptable for v1' gap on Delete Row: an unhandled error here used to block the whole webhook response (same failure class as the Check Budget Alert outage from earlier tonight), taking the entire app offline on a single failed remove instead of just no-op'ing that one action. False branch skips straight to Get Current List/Get Settings so the webhook still returns a valid, unchanged list. Left value uses `|| ""` because the alwaysOutputData placeholder has no row_number key at all (JS undefined), and undefined !== "" would otherwise be true. Wrapped in String(...) because Google Sheets returns row_number as a real number, and this node's strict type validation throws on comparing a number against a string operator rather than silently coercing it (found live 2026-08-08, right after the underlying Find Row to Remove filter itself got fixed).

nodes.name: Delete Row
nodes.notes: Uses row_number returned by the lookup node just before this. If the item wasn't found, this will error — acceptable for v1, revisit with an IF-guard later.

nodes.name: Get Current List
nodes.notes: UPDATED 2026-08-09: executeOnce added -- without it, this re-runs once per input item, so an action producing multiple upstream items (e.g. Recall to ShoppingList upserting N rows) duplicated the whole returned list N times. Should always run exactly once regardless of how many items triggered this shared response path.

nodes.name: Get Settings
nodes.notes: UPDATED 2026-08-09: same executeOnce fix as Get Current List, same reason -- always read Settings exactly once for the shared response path, regardless of upstream item count.

nodes.name: Get Stores
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-11 for online-vs-in-store delivery fee pricing (CLAUDE.md open decision #6). Reads the whole Stores tab once per webhook call so Compute Totals can look up each list store's delivery_fee -- same executeOnce pattern as Get Current List/Get Settings, since this sits on the shared response path regardless of which action triggered it.

nodes.name: Get All ShoppingList Rows
nodes.notes: Reads current row count before clearing -- needed to know how many rows to delete, since we're deliberately avoiding the Google Sheets node's separate 'Clear' operation (its exact parameter shape wasn't verified live, unlike Delete Rows or Columns, which was already fixed and confirmed working tonight for the Remove action). Added 2026-08-08 for the Clear All feature. UPDATED 2026-08-09: added alwaysOutputData -- without it, calling Clear on an already-empty ShoppingList made this node return 0 items, which halts the whole branch right here (n8n's default 'stop when no output data' behavior) rather than reaching Get Current List/Get Settings. Same bug class discovered live via the Recall branch.

nodes.name: Has Rows to Clear?
nodes.notes: Guards against calling Delete Rows or Columns with 0 rows to delete when the list is already empty -- same alwaysOutputData-adjacent defensive pattern used throughout tonight's Check-In Agent fixes, applied proactively here since this is new code. False branch skips straight to Get Current List/Get Settings.

parameters.startIndex: ={{ Math.min(...$('Get All ShoppingList Rows').all().filter(i => i.json && i.json.row_number !== undefined).map(i => i.json.row_number)) }}

nodes.name: Clear ShoppingList Rows
nodes.notes: UPDATED 2026-08-09: Start Row Number changed from a hardcoded 2 to a dynamic expression computing the real minimum row_number from Get All ShoppingList Rows. The hardcoded 2 assumed real data always sits immediately after the header -- broke live when a gap ever formed between the header and the real rows (found during Recall/Snapshot testing), silently deleting the wrong (already-empty) rows and leaving the real stale rows untouched.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (() => { try { if ($('List Webhook').first().json.body.action === 'finalize') return 'true'; if ($('List Webhook').first().json.body.action === 'voice') return String($('Validate Voice Command').first().json.intent === 'finalize'); return 'false'; } catch (e) { return 'false'; } })() }}

nodes.name: Is Finalize?
nodes.notes: Runs in parallel off Compute Totals, alongside the existing (unconditional) connection to Return List + Totals and alongside Check Budget Alert (live-only, not in this checked-in file -- see TODO.md). Uses a named reference all the way back to List Webhook, not bare $json, specifically to avoid the exact wrong-payload-level bug class found and fixed in the Check-In Agent's Read Parsed Reply/Auto-Add to ShoppingList tonight -- Compute Totals' own $json is {list,total,budget,remaining,cadence}, which has no action field of its own. Added 2026-08-08 for the Save List (finalize) feature.

nodes.name: Send Finalize Summary
nodes.notes: On Error MUST be set to Continue on this node (Settings tab) -- an unhandled error here would block the whole webhook response the same way Check Budget Alert did before that was fixed earlier tonight, since this sits on a shared execution even though it's a parallel branch. Use the SAME Telegram bot credential already connected for Budget Alert Listener/Check-In Agent (household chat 1662316637), not a new one.

nodes.name: Get Last Saved List Rows
nodes.notes: UPDATED 2026-08-09: added alwaysOutputData -- an empty LastSavedList (nothing finalized yet) was returning 0 items and halting this branch before Recall to ShoppingList ever ran, which is exactly the silent-death symptom seen live 2026-08-09. New 'Has Last Saved List?' gate right after this node treats the resulting placeholder as 'nothing to recall' instead of blindly upserting a blank row.

nodes.name: Recall to ShoppingList
nodes.notes: Upserts every row from LastSavedList into ShoppingList, matched on item -- merges on top of whatever's already in the list rather than replacing it (per product decision 2026-08-09), same appendOrUpdate pattern as the regular Upsert action. One input item per row (Google Sheets node runs one operation per input item), so N rows in LastSavedList becomes N upserts here. alwaysOutputData is required: if LastSavedList is empty (0 rows in), this node would otherwise produce 0 output items and Get Current List/Get Settings downstream would never fire at all -- same class of bug fixed on Find Row to Remove earlier this project.

nodes.name: Get LastSavedList Rows to Clear
nodes.notes: UPDATED 2026-08-09: alwaysOutputData is required here -- LastSavedList starts out empty, so without this flag this node returned 0 items on every finalize so far, halting this entire branch before Split List for Snapshot/Snapshot to LastSavedList ever ran. Confirmed live: LastSavedList was still empty after two successful Save List taps because of this exact gap.

parameters.startIndex: ={{ Math.min(...$('Get LastSavedList Rows to Clear').all().filter(i => i.json && i.json.row_number !== undefined).map(i => i.json.row_number)) }}

nodes.name: Clear LastSavedList Rows
nodes.notes: UPDATED 2026-08-09: same dynamic-start-row fix as Clear ShoppingList Rows -- the hardcoded startIndex=2 broke live once a gap formed between the header and the real LastSavedList rows (found while testing Recall/Snapshot: two consecutive finalize calls duplicated instead of clearing first). Now computes the real minimum row_number from Get LastSavedList Rows to Clear.

nodes.name: Snapshot to LastSavedList
nodes.notes: Writes the just-finalized list into LastSavedList, one append per item. If Split List for Snapshot produced 0 items (empty list finalized), this simply runs 0 times -- no error.

nodes.name: Has Last Saved List?
nodes.notes: Guards against Recall to ShoppingList upserting a blank/garbage row when Get Last Saved List Rows produced only the alwaysOutputData placeholder (i.e. nothing has ever been finalized yet). Same defensive shape as Found Row to Remove?. Added 2026-08-09.

nodes.name: Get Catalog for Voice
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-11 for voice commands. Reads the whole Catalog tab once per voice request so Build Voice Prompt/Validate Voice Command can fuzzy-match the spoken item name to a real catalog entry (with a real price) instead of letting the LLM invent one.

nodes.name: Parse Voice Command via LLM
nodes.notes: Structured-JSON-only extraction, same discipline as the Price Ingestion Agent's Extract Receipt via LLM.

nodes.name: Voice Item Matched?
nodes.notes: True branch upserts the resolved catalog match. False branch (spoken item didn't match anything in the catalog) skips the sheet write entirely -- never invent a price -- and Compute Totals' voiceReply tells the user to add it via Browse Catalog or a receipt scan instead.

nodes.name: Get Catalog for Barcode
nodes.notes: Live-drift resync (2026-08-15): reconstructed from the live workflow, which was built directly in n8n rather than scaffolded here first (see TODO.md's 2026-08-15 entries). Unfiltered read -- Match Barcode does the barcode comparison client-side over every Catalog row.

nodes.name: Lookup Barcode via UPCitemdb
nodes.notes: UPCitemdb trial tier: no API key, ~100 lookups/day, coverage inconsistent -- treated as unverified/live data downstream (see Shape External Barcode Result), never merged into Catalog automatically.

nodes.name: Get Settings for Budget Update
nodes.notes: Live-drift resync (2026-08-15): reconstructed from the live workflow (see TODO.md's 2026-08-15 entries). Unfiltered read of the single-row Settings tab.

nodes.name: Update Settings Budget
nodes.notes: Writes budget from the request body; every other Settings column is written back unchanged from the row just read (Get Settings for Budget Update), since Update Row overwrites every mapped column. On Error: Continue so a write hiccup here still lets the shared Get Current List/Get Settings response path run.

nodes.name: Find Catalog Row for Log Price
nodes.notes: In-store price log (added 2026-08-15, scaffolded in repo -- not yet applied live in n8n). Filters Catalog on item AND store (two filtersUI entries = AND, same as every other multi-condition Sheets filter in this workflow). alwaysOutputData: true because a new item/store combo the scanner hasn't seen before is a normal case, not an error -- same reasoning as Find Row to Remove.

nodes.name: Has Existing Catalog Row?
nodes.notes: Same String(...||"") pattern as Found Row to Remove?/Has Last Saved List? -- the alwaysOutputData placeholder has no row_number key at all, and bare undefined !== "" would otherwise be true. True: an existing Catalog row for this item+store gets its price updated directly (in-store scan is treated as higher-confidence than a web scrape, so it skips the Price Refresh Agent's 24-48h freshness gate). False: a brand-new item/store combo gets appended fresh.

nodes.name: Update Catalog Price
nodes.notes: Matched on row_number from Find Catalog Row for Log Price (passes straight through the IF gate as $json here). Deliberately leaves size/unit_price/unit_label alone -- an in-store price confirmation doesn't tell us pack size, so overwriting those would be guessing. barcode backfills only if the row didn't already have one (|| $json.barcode keeps the existing value otherwise). Sourced from $('List Webhook') for the submitted price/barcode, not bare $json, since $json here is the Catalog row, not the request body -- same nested-payload discipline as everywhere else in this workflow.

nodes.name: Append New Catalog Row
nodes.notes: New item/store combo not previously in Catalog. Sourced entirely from $('List Webhook') rather than bare $json -- at this point $json is Find Catalog Row for Log Price's alwaysOutputData placeholder (no real data), not the request body. item/category are required in the request body per the frontend contract: never silently guess a name/category for an unrecognized barcode.

nodes.name: Append to PriceLog
nodes.notes: Both the update and append Catalog branches converge here -- always logs a historical PriceLog row regardless of which one ran. status: 'confirmed' (not 'pending') because an in-store human-read price bypasses the Price Refresh Agent's 24-48h freshness gate entirely -- it's already higher-confidence than a scrape. Sourced from $('List Webhook'), same reasoning as the two nodes above -- $json here is whichever Catalog write just ran, not the request body.

parameters.jsCode:
const body = $('List Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { ok: true, item: body.item, store: body.store, price: Number(body.price) } }];

nodes.name: Log Price Response
nodes.notes: Dedicated response, deliberately not routed through Get Current List/Compute Totals -- this action never touches ShoppingList, so there's nothing to gain from the shared list/budget response path, and this avoids editing Compute Totals' existing jsCode at all.

nodes.name: Find Store Row
nodes.notes: Auto-geolocated store setup (added 2026-08-15, scaffolded in repo -- not yet applied live in n8n). alwaysOutputData: true so a genuine no-match doesn't halt the branch -- Store Row Found? right after turns that into a clean error response instead of an unhandled error.

nodes.name: Store Row Found?
nodes.notes: Same String(...||"") pattern as Found Row to Remove?. False: an unrecognized store name returns a clean error rather than silently creating a new Stores row from a location ping -- new stores go through explicit store setup, not this action.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ok: false, error: 'unknown store' } }];

nodes.name: Update Store Row
nodes.notes: Writes lat/long only. Runs in parallel with the address-resolution branch below (Has Existing Address? onward) -- that branch is what actually fills address in, gated so it only ever runs when the column was genuinely blank, per the spec's 'never overwrite a manually-entered address' rule.

nodes.name: Has Existing Address?
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-15 (v2 scaffold, not yet applied live) once the Geocoding API was confirmed enabled on the project's Google Cloud project. Gates the whole reverse-geocode branch below on address already being blank -- structurally guarantees 'never overwrite a manually-entered address' rather than relying on the geocode call itself to be careful. Same ternary-to-string pattern as Has Existing Catalog Row? (log_price branch, fixed earlier the same day) instead of a bare not-equals-empty-string check, since that exact shape silently misbehaved on an unset value that day.

parameters.jsCode:
const row = $('Find Store Row').first().json;
return [{ json: { address: row.address } }];

nodes.name: Keep Existing Address
nodes.notes: True branch of Has Existing Address? -- address already on file, pass it through unchanged rather than re-geocoding it.

nodes.name: Reverse Geocode via Google Maps
nodes.notes: Reuses the same Query Auth credential already confirmed live for the Recommendation Agent's Distance Matrix calls (id jGUkE00XLHIOjbD4 -- holds the shared Google Maps Platform API key as query param 'key'). Geocoding API confirmed enabled on the same GCP project 2026-08-15, so no new credential is needed -- but its display name ('Google Distance Matrix API') is now a little misleading since it backs two different APIs; worth a rename live for clarity, not a blocker. onError: continueRegularOutput so a geocode failure (bad coordinates, API hiccup) degrades to a blank address instead of failing update_store_location entirely -- lat/long, the primary ask, are already written by the parallel Update Store Row branch regardless of how this branch goes.

nodes.name: Parse Geocode Result
nodes.notes: A non-OK status (ZERO_RESULTS, INVALID_REQUEST, etc.) or the onError continue-output shape from the HTTP node above both fall through to address: null here -- same non-throwing degrade-gracefully behavior as the Recommendation Agent's own Parse Distance + Est Trip Cost node.

nodes.name: Geocode Succeeded?
nodes.notes: False branch (geocode failed or returned no results) skips the sheet write and goes straight to Format Update Store Location Response -- address just stays blank for this run, same as if the geocode branch hadn't fired at all.

nodes.name: Update Store Address
nodes.notes: Writes only row_number/address (matched on row_number, same as Update Store Row) -- doesn't touch lat/long, so this can run in parallel with Update Store Row without either clobbering the other's columns. row_number is pulled by name from Find Store Row since $json at this point is Parse Geocode Result's output, not the sheet row.

parameters.jsCode:
const body = $('List Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { ok: true, store: body.store, lat: body.lat, long: body.long, address: $json.address || null } }];

nodes.name: Format Update Store Location Response
nodes.notes: address now reflects the real result of the address-resolution branch (Keep Existing Address / Update Store Address / a failed Geocode Succeeded?) via $json, rather than always echoing Find Store Row's original pre-write snapshot -- whichever of those three nodes actually fed this node's input this run determines the value. lat/long are still echoed straight from the request body, matching Update Store Row's write.

nodes.name: Find Store Row for Add
nodes.notes: Add a new store (added 2026-08-16). Filters Stores on store name to check for a duplicate before appending -- same alwaysOutputData reasoning as Find Store Row: a genuine no-match (the normal, expected case -- this store doesn't exist yet) shouldn't halt the branch.

nodes.name: Store Already Exists?
nodes.notes: Same ternary-to-string pattern as Has Existing Catalog Row?/Geocode Succeeded? (both fixed live 2026-08-15 after the bare String(...||"") pattern misbehaved on unset values that day) -- used here from the start rather than repeating that lesson. True: a store with this exact name already has a row -- reject rather than silently creating a duplicate. False: genuinely new store name, safe to append.

parameters.jsCode:
const body = $('List Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { ok: false, error: `Store already exists: ${body.store}` } }];

nodes.name: Append New Store Row
nodes.notes: New store, name only -- address/lat/long/distance/est_trip_cost/delivery_fee all start blank, matching how every other store row begins (address gets filled later via update_store_location v2's reverse-geocode, or by hand; distance_from_home_mi/est_trip_cost by the Recommendation Agent's geocoding chain once Settings.home_address is set). channel defaults to 'in-store' -- the common case for a store someone's adding while physically standing in it; an online-only channel row is still easiest to add by hand directly in the Sheet, same as today.

parameters.jsCode:
const body = $('List Webhook').first().json.body;
return [{ json: { ok: true, store: body.store } }];

main.node: Find Catalog Row for Log Price
